transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-20 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Redwood CSM), Sasha Nguyen (Lagoon CTO), Marta Ruiz (Lagoon Head of ML), Evan Cole (Lagoon Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff for Lagoon Med to align on objectives, infra requirements (VPC/SSO), Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, and next-step pilot tasks. Agreed to set up a dev account and run initial throughput benchmarks.

Topics:
- Objectives and success criteria
- Security / SSO and compliance requirements
- Network / VPC connectivity and IP allowlisting
- Dedicated capacity sizing and quantization options
- Pilot timeline and deliverables

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for carving time, i'm Jordan with Redwood, i'm the CSM lead for this onboarding, um we're gonna run through objectives and next steps - priya and alex from my team are here to cover the technical side and ops.
[00:12] Sasha Nguyen: thanks, jordan. excited to get going. we've got aggressive timelines here, q1 production target so we wanna understand latency and cost tradeoffs.
[00:25] Priya Patel: great, uh quick intro from me - i'm priya, solutions engineer, i'll own the architecture and benchmarking for the pilot. happy to dig into dedicated pool sizing and the VPC options.
[00:38] Marta Ruiz: and i'm marta, head of ml, we'll be feeding anonymized clinical notes into the models, so data residency and audit logs are important for us.
[00:50] Evan Cole: evan here - platform team, i'll be responsible for network and onboarding the service into our stack.
[00:55] Jordan Lee: awesome. first up, success criteria - sasha, marta, can you share what success looks like for lagoon?
[01:05] Sasha Nguyen: yeah. number one is sub-200ms median token latency for our interactive assistant use-case, number two is cost per 1k tokens in target range - we have some budget constraints - and three, SOC2-level audit trails and SSO/saml with SCIM for user provisioning.
[01:25] Priya Patel: ok we're hearing latency, cost, and compliance. for latency, depending on model and quantization we can hit sub-200ms on dedicated pools for shorter sequences. for hosted there's more variance but it's faster to iterate.
[01:40] Jordan Lee: just to add, we usually recommend starting hosted for quick validation then move to dedicated for production predictability, but if you need VPC and no egress, private deploy is an option.
[01:54] Marta Ruiz: can you clarify private deploy? we might need on-prem for a subset of data later. is that something you support?
[02:02] Alex Rivera: yes, we have private (VPC and on-prem) options, there is an additional platform fee and longer lead time. for now pilot we'd suggest dedicated in your cloud region to validate performance.
[02:18] Evan Cole: how intrusive is the network setup? we run strict egress rules.
[02:22] Priya Patel: typical pattern is a customer-managed VPC peering or private-link style connectivity, plus allowlisting a small set of egress IPs. we'll share network diagrams and a checklist.
[02:34] Sasha Nguyen: ok that's helpful. security - do you support customer-managed KMS for key encryption?
[02:40] Jordan Lee: yes, KM S support with BYOK is available for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports envelope encryption but we can integrate with KMS for enterprise contracts.
[02:50] Marta Ruiz: audit logs - retention? we need 12 months.
[02:53] Alex Rivera: we can set log retention per contract, and we also have per-token traceability features in the console. we'll share the SOC2/ISO and audit docs in the welcome packet.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: right, i'll attach the security pack after the call.
[03:12] Priya Patel: moving to architecture - for your workload (clinical QA + summarization), we typically recommend a mix: smaller quantized model for embeddings and reranking, and a stronger float/half model for generation. Quantization lowers cost but can affect quality.
[03:28] Marta Ruiz: yeah quality is critical - for clinical text we need to avoid hallucinations. how do you help monitor regressions?
[03:34] Priya Patel: we have a quality monitoring feature that ties to eval sets. we'll onboard a small eval prompt set and run daily checks; if quality drops we'll trigger alerts and can roll back to previous model versions.
[03:45] Sasha Nguyen: curious about throughput - our spike patterns are predictable but bursty during morning triage. how does autoscaling behave with Dedicated?
[03:55] Priya Patel: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies plus burst capacity options. autoscale is based on queue depth and latency SLOs, it can spin up additional workers in the pool - we usually recommend some buffer for predictable spikes.
[04:10] Evan Cole: cost model - is it per-token on Hosted and per-hour on Dedicated?
[04:15] Jordan Lee: hosted is per-token + embedding units. Dedicated is committed capacity monthly + lower per-token unit. we'll include pricing scenarios in the deck.
[04:25] Sasha Nguyen: any existing integrations for SSO? we use Okta.
[04:29] Alex Rivera: yes Okta SAML + SCIM is supported; we'll share an Okta guide.
[04:34] Jordan Lee: quick note: i may have spoken with a different priya earlier - small name collision, ha - the one on your side is fine, we'll label them in notes.
[04:42] (laughter)
[04:45] Priya (customer): yep, that's me.
[04:48] Jordan Lee: next, pilot plan proposal - priya (redwood) do you want to walk through recommended deliverables and timeline?
[04:55] Priya Patel (Redwood SE): sure. week 0-1: provisioning dev project + seed dataset; week 2: run baseline benchmarks (latency/cost) with our reference prompts; week 3-4: iterate model/configs and run quality evals; week 5: present findings and recommended Dedicated sizing. timeline flexible but target to have production-ready recommendations by early q1.
[05:20] Marta Ruiz: sounds good. what do you need from us to get started?
[05:24] Priya Patel: access to a small sample of anonymized notes, expected traffic profiles (qps, seq length distribution), and network contacts for allowlist. also SSO admin for test user provisioning.
[05:36] Evan Cole: i'll gather the network reqs and share IPs.
[05:39] Sasha Nguyen: i'll own the success criteria and sign-off.
[05:43] Jordan Lee: perfect. i'll send the welcome packet after this call with links: onboarding deck, security pack, Okta guide, network checklist, and a demo credentials set for the dev account.
[05:56] Priya Patel: one note on benchmarks - for clinical workloads you might prioritize throughput with a mid-sized quantized model then validate quality. we'll propose two configs: cost-optimized and latency-optimized.
[06:10] Marta Ruiz: can you share previous benchmark numbers or a spreadsheet?
[06:14] Priya Patel: yes i will drop a sample benchmark spreadsheet and our model performance profiles - link will be in the follow up.
[06:20] Sasha Nguyen: any blocker on compliance? we require SOC2 and contractual audit clauses for patient data - do you have a process for sub-processors?
[06:30] Alex Rivera: yes we document subprocessors and can include contractual terms in our enterprise agreement. security team can run an assessment if needed.
[06:38] Evan Cole: would a POC require a separate legal NDA?
[06:42] Jordan Lee: no separate NDA required for the pilot, we operate under the standard master services agreement; but we can fast-track an MSA if procurement needs it.
[06:52] Sasha Nguyen: procurement will want a ballpark for committed dollars if we go Dedicated - can you provide tiered pricing?
[06:58] Jordan Lee: yes we'll send tiered pricing scenarios in the deck - committed monthly vs hosted pay-as-you-go estimates.
[07:06] (background noise)
[07:12] Priya Patel: ok i want to call out one technical risk: KV cache warmup for long sequences might affect p99 latency early on. we'll instrument the cache and provide suggestions - smaller batch sizes for cold-starts.
[07:26] Marta Ruiz: good to know. also anonymization - we may need redaction at ingestion time, any recommended patterns?
[07:33] Priya Patel: yes best practice is client-side redaction + tokenization and then send pseudonymized payloads. we can share examples.
[07:42] Jordan Lee: to summarize actions: jordan send docs, priya share benchmarks and schedule deep-dive, evan share network details. agreed?
[07:52] Sasha Nguyen: agreed.
[07:54] Evan Cole: agreed.
[07:56] Jordan Lee: ok last part, who is the day-to-day contact for lagoon?
[07:59] Sasha Nguyen: sasha will be final sign-off, but evan will be day-to-day for infra and marta for ml questions.
[08:09] Jordan Lee: perfect. i'll schedule the architecture deep-dive for next week, priya will send calendar hold.
[08:16] Priya Patel: will do.
[08:18] Alex Rivera: i'll also include the customer success plan and milestones in the invite.
[08:22] (brief crosstalk)
[08:30] Jordan Lee: any final q's?
[08:33] Marta Ruiz: none from me.
[08:34] Sasha Nguyen: all good. thanks everyone.
[08:36] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and action items. talk soon.

End of recording.
